'''Shimosuwa Aozuka Kofun''' (下諏訪青塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|qid=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Shimosuwa|en|Shimosuwa|qid=Q1204211|lt=Shimosuwa, Nagano}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}, Japan. Its type is that of a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun}}, and it is Historic Site1 as a historic site by Nagano Prefecture.

== Overview ==
The Kofun was constructed on the tip of a hill projecting westward in the northern region of {{ill|Lake Suwa|en|Lake Suwa|qid=Q1206692|lt=Lake Suwa}}. It is situated near the {{ill|Shimosha Akimiya|ja|諏訪大社下社秋宮}} of {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa Taisha}}. The site is within the shrine's property, and parts of the mound (especially the eastern side) have been eroded by surrounding developments. The {{ill|Aozuka Shrine|ja|青塚社}}, a subsidiary shrine of Suwa Taisha, is located in the western constriction area of the mound.

The kofun is keyhole-shaped with its front part oriented to the north-northwest. It is the only keyhole-shaped Kofun in the Suwa region and belongs to the late phase of this style. {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪}} have been discovered on the mound's surface, making it the only example in the Suwa region where haniwa have been found. Historical records from the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} mention the discovery of human-shaped haniwa, which were later reburied, though recent investigations have found no items other than cylindrical haniwa. 

The burial facility is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/horizontal stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} exposed and open on the western constriction area of the rear mound, approximately five meters above the base level. The chamber is constructed with natural {{ill|Andesite|en|Andesite|qid=Q181908|lt=andesite}} stones in a random stone masonry style. It measures 5.5 meters in total length. Although the corridor leading to the chamber has been destroyed, it is presumed to have been a double-chambered type. Few burial goods from the chamber are known.

The Aozuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late 6th century. Scholars suggest links to the {{ill|Kanasashi clan|ja|金刺氏}}, the ritualist family of Suwa Taisha's Shimosha, and connections with other keyhole-shaped Kofuns distributed along the {{ill|Tenryū River|en|Tenryū River|qid=Q13667|lt=Tenryu River}}. This makes the mound an important archaeological site for studying the political landscape of ancient Suwa.

The Kofun was Historic Site1 as a Nagano Prefecture historic site in 1965.

== Mound ==
The mound's area are as follows:
* Mound length: 57 meters
* Rear part:
''' Diameter: 34 meters (estimated reconstruction)
''' Height: 8.1 meters
* Front part:
''' Width: 40 meters (estimated reconstruction)
''' Height: 8 meters

According to the site's intypeation board, the primary axis length is 67 meters, the rear part's diameter is 33.4 meters, and the front part's width is 42.8 meters.
